newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium 1997 budget effort 100 bln Bfr - paper.
newsitem.headline: Belgium 1997 budget effort 100 bln Bfr - paper.

text.p: Belgium will shave 100 billion Belgian francs off its 1997 budget, with a third coming from increased taxes, newspaper Le Soir reported on Friday.
Le Soir said the budget package would contain 32 billion francs of new tax measures, 31 billion francs of social security cuts and 37 billion francs of non fiscal receipts drawn from various sources.
A spokeswoman for Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene declined to confirm the figures.
The government must find more savings in order to meet the budget criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
Budget talks started before the summer and are due to finish at the end of September, before the traditional state of the union address to parliament on October 1.
But work by senior ministers was interrupted this week upon discovery of the bodies of two more dead children in the country's widening paedophile scandal.
Talks are likely to be suspended again this weekend while the funerals of the two children take place.
